newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean worker in Kuwait defects to South Korea.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean worker in Kuwait defects to South Korea.

text.p: A North Korean construction worker in Kuwait who sought asylum to South Korea will arrive in Seoul on Thursday, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.

Spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung said 29-year-old Lim Jae-il arrived at the South Korean embassy in Kuwait last week. His defection was approved after officials from Kuwait and the United Nations High Commissioner confirmed Lim's desire to defect.
Lee said the defector already left Kuwait and was coming to South Korea via Europe. He added that about 1,500 North Koreans work in construction sites in Kuwait.
A statement by the ministry said Lim had worked in Kuwait since last November.

South Korea is awaiting the arrival of Pyongyang's highest-ranking defector, Hwang Jang-yop, who was flown to the Philippines last week from Beijing after almost five weeks of sheltering at a South Korean mission.
More than 600 North Korean defectors now live in South Korea.
A string of defections in recent months has been prompted by food shortages and economic collapse in the impoverished North.
On Tuesday South Korea's intelligence agency said three North Koreans were also seeking asylum to South Korea from a third country. Details concerning their defection were not provided.
Last December, 17 members of a single family defected to South Korea through Hong Kong, the largest single group to seek asylum since the 1950-53 Korean War.
In January, eight North Koreans from two families came to the South by boat via China.
